newsitem.title: USA: Venture in compliance with bank covenants.
newsitem.headline: Venture in compliance with bank covenants.

text.p: Venture Stores Inc said Thursday it was in compliance with all of its bank covenants, and proceeds from a sale-leaseback deal and store sales would provide funding for its repositioning program.
"Venture has taken major steps to lay the groundwork for improved future performance," Robert Wildrick, chairman and chief executive, said in a statement.
The retailer has sold and closed 20 unprofitable stores for $38 million. In addition it has closed on a $135 million sale-leaseback agreement with Kimco Realty Corp.

"These two initiatives, with a combined value of about $173 million, will help improve performance and provide a substantial cash infusion to help support our continuing repositioning," Wildrick said. The 20 stores being sold accounted for about 40 percent of Venture's 1996 pre-tax loss.

The 13 weeks ended July 26, 1997 included a nonrecurring charge of $63.9 million, or $3.50 a share, for costs associated the store closings, including a loss of $1.34 per share of unrealizable deferred tax benefits. Including this charge, the second quarter 1997 net loss applicable to common shareholders was $103.6 million, or $5.67 per share.
After the closing of the 20 stores, Venture will operate 93 family value stores in nine states.

Total sales fell 0.3 percent in the second quarter to $328.5 million. Still, Wildrick said Venture is encouraged by the continued improvement in the company's total sales over the past few months. Venture's total sales rose during June and July.

The results for the quarter were in the range previously forecast by the company and were hurt by tighter credit limits and an interruption in merchandise flow, particularly apparel, which had a negative impact on the merchandise mix and margins during the period.
